Sangchu Geotjeori Fresh Lettuce Salad

Sangchu geotjeori takes the same lettuce that wraps the ssam (#F01) and dresses half a head of it as a quick, spicy, unfermented salad — the fresh-kimchi treatment (#B04's logic) run on the leaf.

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: heritage — the lettuce bowl beyond the wrap. Sangchu geotjeori takes the same lettuce that wraps the ssam (#F01) and dresses half a head of it as a quick, spicy, unfermented salad — the fresh-kimchi treatment (#B04's logic) run on the leaf. It is the lightest red bowl on the table, five minutes of work, and the one that makes a simple rice-and-meat lunch feel complete.

The lettuce

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Tear, don't cut — cut lettuce edges brown and weep; torn edges hold. Spin completely dry, the #F01 law again: water on the leaf dilutes the dressing into a puddle.
  • Hold the dressing and the lettuce separate until serving — this bowl dresses at the table's start and eats within the hour.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    The dressing stirred together in the serving bowl — gochugaru, soy, honey, garlic — into a loose paste. Checkpoint — tastes a shade too strong on a fingertip; the lettuce's water will round it, same law as every fresh bowl in this family.
  2. 02
    Lettuce in, tossed with two spoons or hands — #B04's massage minute — until every leaf wears the red-flecked gloss. Sesame oil, seeds, scallion over. Checkpoint — the leaf test: crisp, cold, dressed-through — spicy-savory on the first bite, the leaf's clean sweetness after, no dressing pooling at the bowl's floor. Serve beside any of the M-list's records; it is the freshest possible counter to the gochujang lanes (#M04, #M13). Chef’s Note — the geotjeori family (#B04, this bowl, #F05's slaw) is the Korean table's answer to the everyday problem of wanting kimchi's flavor on a day the jar is empty or the meal wants lightness — every vegetable that holds water can take the fresh treatment, and lettuce is the most delicate and fastest of them. The family's shared law: dress strong, dress late, eat early.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Dressing pooled at the bottomWet lettuce or early dressingBone-dry leaves; dress at serving
Leaves wiltedSat too long dressedInside the hour, always
Bland leavesDressed to target, not pastA notch strong before the toss
Browning edgesKnife-cut lettuceTear by hand

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Undressed lettuce keeps 2 days in paper towel; the dressed bowl does not keep — by design.
  • Variations: cucumber pieces folded in; the cabbage version (#B04) for a sturdier bowl; a drop of cho-gochujang (#SA03) thinned as the dressing for the sweet-heat fork.
